_note: R2 (2026-11-09), see mesen2-results/R2_20261109.md. Scene sweep of ROM O (ids $01-$FF written into sceneNext, 231 load, 24 never finish) and a no-record test of ROM R. Shipped sentences made wrong or incomplete: the 25 ids without a scene script record can be written into sceneNext but never load a room (23 hang, $09 and $80 run stray bytes, R crashes in all 25); scene_actors says nothing of what the 16 shared-default ids do; the scene_warps data facts leave the pan-list use, the walk of the two warp_def_03 entries and the save-warp records untraced; scanline_band_hdma_thinker counts scene $84 (not loadable) among the 81 parallax scenes and does not mention the unreferenced $0F spawn; game_over_sequence states which record each path reads but not that it was measured; display_preset_table does not say how the preset is chosen or used. Dry-run only: npm run merge -- plans/extracted-audit/mesen2-results/specs/R2_notes.json --dry-run. The flag $FF comment (scene_lifecycle 253564) is covered by specs/W1-b_notes.json; the sweep adds no further edit to it (every flag $FF test of the 231 loadable scenes comes from a thinker slot).

edit.find: 15 of the 16 unused ids of scene_actors are in that list.
edit.with: 15 of the 16 unused ids of scene_actors are in that list. No warp, QueueMapChange operand or script names any of the 25 ids, and none of them loads a room when it is written into sceneNext ($0642). In the original ROM FindCurrentScene scans the whole script block for the id: for 23 ids it finds no match and never returns (the NMI count stops after 17 frames; 18 ids stay in the scan loop, 5 run stray code), and $09 and $80 match a stray byte and run the bytes after it as a script (no SceneCmd_ConfigDisplay runs; $09 leaves a collision map of 3072 cells of type $0E, $80 keeps the previous scene's map). The rebuilt layout reads a $0000 pointer from scene_meta_list for these ids, so FindCurrentScene returns Y = $0000 - $3A, far from any record, and the interpreter runs whatever bytes lie there as commands: the game crashes for all 25 (the NMI stops after 19 frames with the stack pointer at $4212).

edit.find: No scene-warp destination and no QueueMapChange operand names any of those ids.
edit.with: No scene-warp destination and no QueueMapChange operand names any of those ids. Writing one into sceneNext ($0642) of the original ROM does not show a TEST MAP: $48 $57 $76 $77 $81 $9E $AA $AB $AF $C1 $C2 $CA $CB $F8 have no scene script record and the load never finishes, $80 runs stray bytes as a script, and $F9 (which has a script record with display preset $00) never leaves the wait loop at ROM 166828 that reads APUIO0 until it is $00. The rebuilt ROM loads $F9 and crashes for the others.

edit.find: The two forced-walk entries of warp_def_03 use unusual first stream bytes ($04, $05); not traced: what the walk does with them.
edit.with: The two forced-walk entries of warp_def_03 use the first stream bytes $04 (south) and $05 (north), which are rows of walk_step_table identical to $02 and $00 (animation 9; move chain $14 and $12). Measured in scenes $03 and $04: all four entries stage the same step word ($1409 south, $1209 north) and pan the camera the same 256 px (list $00); the two warp_def_03 entries differ only in their longer Y offset (+328 / -304 px instead of +264 / -240).

edit.find: GameOverSequence reloads a warp from the entry+4 pointer stored in reviveWarpPtr ($0AF4; every warp) and sceneSaveData (save warps).
edit.with: GameOverSequence reloads a warp from the entry+4 pointer stored in reviveWarpPtr ($0AF4; every warp, measured on 32 entries) and sceneSaveData ($0AF0; the 23 save warps, which also store it in reviveWarpPtr; the 9 non-save warps tested leave $0AF0 and $0AF2 at 0). The 23 save warps lie in 14 scenes ($1A $1C $24 $4C x4 $5E $6B $88 $B1 $B7 $CC x7 $DF $E1 $E2 $E3) and lead into the Moon Tribe cave, Larai Cliff, the four Sky Garden wings, the Mu entrance, the Angel Village tunnel, the Great Wall Sand Fanger lair, the Angkor Wat courtyards, seven Pyramid rooms and the Babel Tower floors. With 0 gems a game over lands at the last save warp's record (measured: save warp $1A to $1B, then plain warp $24 to $22, game over: scene $1B); with 100 gems the respawn lands at the last warp's record ($22).
